title: Meteor showers
summary: Hours of frames to catch a few bright streaks.

media.alt: Dozens of meteor streaks over the Milky Way and a desert ridge, several frames stacked

blocks.note: Same as the Milky Way, then shoot non-stop for hours.

head: Shower
Peak
Notes
rows: Warm nights, lots of bright ones

steps: Check the peak night and the Moon. A bright Moon washes out all but the brightest meteors.
Go dark, away from towns. Best hours are usually after midnight.
Wide lens on a tripod. Aim about halfway up the sky, a little to the side of where the shower comes from.
Milky Way settings: widest aperture, ISO 3200, shutter from the 500 rule. Manual focus on a bright star.
Interval timer on, unlimited shots, long-exposure noise reduction off.
Let it run for hours. Then pick the frames with meteors, and stack them over one background if you like.

items: Meteors are random. The more frames, the more you catch.
Dew forms on the lens on clear nights. A hand warmer strapped to the barrel keeps it clear.

steps: **Mode dial to M**. Aperture wide open, **ISO 3200**, shutter from the star calculator (about 17 s at 18 mm).
Switch to **MF** and focus on a bright star in magnified live view.
Lens IS off on the tripod: the R10 has no in-body stabiliser, so the lens switch is the one that matters.
**Shooting 7 › Interval timer › Enable**. Interval 2 s longer than the shutter, shots **00**.
Press the shutter fully to start. A full battery lasts a few hours in the cold at most: have the spare ready.
